___ is an ___ year old woman with a history of afib on 
coumadin (with recent supra-therapeutic INRs) who presents with 
an occipital SAH and intraventricular extension felt to be 
secondary to RCVS.

- She was initially seen by neurosurgery who did not recommend 
surgical management.

She was admitted to the ICU overnight for 
close monitoring.

She did not require any gtt for blood pressure 
control and she was transferred to the floor with no 
issues.Given her presentation and appearance of her SAH on 
imaging, ddx was primarily RCVS vs Amyloid angiopathy with 
resultant SAH.

Her brain MRI did not reveal any further 
evidence of Amyloid Angiopathy and RVCS was favored.

She was 
started on Verapamil- initially 40mg PO TID for 
treatment/preventions of RCVS but subsequently transitioned to

Sustained Release 120mg prior to discharge. ___ headaches 
were well controlled with PO tylenol and gabapentin 100 mg TID.
- Following discharge, the plan was to have her undergo a

Should it be stable 
or resolving, after discussion with Dr. ___ will 
likely be started on therapeutic anticoagulation for her atrial 
fibrillation.

Risk of recurrence of this issue is likely low as 
long as possible precipitants are avoided.

- Possible precipitants of her RCVS include SSRIs (i.e., 
citalopram), some sleep medications (i.e., trazodone) stimulants 
such as in Cough medicines  with decongestants as this may 
worsen or even 
cause episodes of RCVS

No changes were 
made to her beta blocker regimen.
- Losartan was increased to 100mg PO Daily.
